messages.content:
Terms extracted from wound-care abstracts were placed under classes of a wound
ontology (WONT, built on MILD, OBO modules and BFO 2020) as a KIND of the class
(is_a). A check then asked whether a term is in fact only a restatement of its
class: another name for exactly the same thing ("C" placed under "carbon atom").

Decide for EVERY row how the TERM stands to the CLASS:
- "same": the term names exactly the class; it is another name for it
  (spelling, plural, abbreviation, word order, a synonym).
- "narrower": the term names a genuine kind of the class: it adds a qualifier,
  or names a particular member, scale, grade, organism or substance
  ("herpes simplex virus" under "Viruses", "frostbite injury" under "Thermal wound").
- "broader": the class is a kind of what the term names; the term is the more
  general of the two ("wound" placed under "chronic wound").
- "different": none of these: a part, a measure, a process or a property
  related to the class, or another thing.

Read the class's definition where given. Give one sentence of reason for every row.

ROWS

ROW 1: TERM "height" (in 13 abstracts) placed under CLASS "1-D extent" (quality). Definition: A size quality inhering in an bearer by virtue of the bearer's extension in one dimension.
   The check said "same": Height is a one-dimensional extent, synonymous with the class.
ROW 2: TERM "vascular disorder" (in 8 abstracts) placed under CLASS "Angiopathy" (material entity). Definition: A pathological disorder consisting in an abnormal structure of the wall or of the lumen of one or more blood vessels, such that perfusion of the tissue those vessels supply is reduced.
   The check said "unclear": Vascular disorder is broader than angiopathy; placement as subclass is ambiguous without context.
ROW 3: TERM "degree of burn" (in 3 abstracts) placed under CLASS "Burn classification grade" (information entity). Definition: A wound classification grade that is a category of the burn classification scale.
   The check said "same": "Degree of burn" is essentially another name for a burn classification grade, denoting the severity level.

   The check said "same": Vaseline gauze is a common name for cellulose acetate mesh impregnated with a petrolatum emulsion.

   The check said "unclear": Non-healing lesion is broader than chronic wound; placement as subclass is questionable; cannot determine intended meaning.
ROW 6: TERM "long-standing ulcer" (in 2 abstracts) placed under CLASS "Chronic wound" (material entity). Definition: A wound that has failed to progress through the phases of healing in an orderly and timely fashion.
   The check said "same": Long-standing ulcer is essentially synonymous with chronic wound.

ROW 8: TERM "persistent wound" (in 2 abstracts) placed under CLASS "Chronic wound" (material entity). Definition: A wound that has failed to progress through the phases of healing in an orderly and timely fashion.
   The check said "same": Persistent wound is essentially a synonym for chronic wound.
ROW 9: TERM "slow-healing wound" (in 2 abstracts) placed under CLASS "Chronic wound" (material entity). Definition: A wound that has failed to progress through the phases of healing in an orderly and timely fashion.
   The check said "same": Slow-healing wound is synonymous with chronic wound.
ROW 10: TERM "exposed tendon" (in 5 abstracts) placed under CLASS "Deep wound" (material entity). Definition: A wound that bears the quality increased depth: it extends further into the tissue than is typical for a wound of its kind.
   The check said "unclear": Exposed tendon is a condition or feature, not a type of wound.
ROW 11: TERM "diabetes-related foot ulcer" (in 25 abstracts) placed under CLASS "Diabetic foot ulcer" (material entity). Definition: A diabetic wound that is located in a foot.
   The check said "same": Diabetes-related foot ulcer is a synonym for diabetic foot ulcer.
ROW 12: TERM "diabetic disorder" (in 9 abstracts) placed under CLASS "Diabetic metabolic disorder" (material entity). Definition: A pathological disorder consisting in the abnormal organization of the insulin-secreting or insulin-responsive tissues of a patient, such that glucose homeostasis is not maintained.
   The check said "unclear": Diabetic disorder is broader than Diabetic metabolic disorder (it includes non-metabolic complications), so it is not a genuine subclass; it may be a misplacement.
ROW 13: TERM "prediabete" (in 3 abstracts) placed under CLASS "Diabetic metabolic disorder" (material entity). Definition: A pathological disorder consisting in the abnormal organization of the insulin-secreting or insulin-responsive tissues of a patient, such that glucose homeostasis is not maintained.
   The check said "unclear": Prediabete (likely prediabetes) is not a diabetic metabolic disorder in the same sense; it is a precursor state, so it is unclear if it should be a subclass or a separate entity.
ROW 14: TERM "work-up" (in 4 abstracts) placed under CLASS "Disease diagnostic process" (process). Definition: A planned process that has as output a disease diagnostic result.
   The check said "same": Work-up is a common synonym for a disease diagnostic process.
ROW 15: TERM "treating" (in 16 abstracts) placed under CLASS "Disease disorder treatment process" (process). Definition: A planned process that realizes a treatment plan and that has as input a pathological disorder that is part of a material disease entity.
   The check said "same": Treating is essentially synonymous with the process of treating a disease or disorder.

   The check said "same": Hyperplasia of scar is essentially the same as hypertrophic scar.

   The check said "unclear": Impaired healing process may be broader than or synonymous with impaired wound healing process; relationship ambiguous.

   The check said "same": Aberrant wound-healing process is another way to say impaired wound healing process.
ROW 23: TERM "aberrant wound healing response" (in 3 abstracts) placed under CLASS "Impaired wound healing process" (process). (no definition)
   The check said "same": Aberrant wound healing response is another way to say impaired wound healing process.
